mainTopic: The מן and the שליו in the מדבר: mealtimes, reconciling פסוקים, the quail stories, and whether the מן left any waste
overview: The גמרא continues discussing the מן and the שליו that ישראל ate in the מדבר. The bread was requested properly, so it came properly in the morning. From the meat coming at night, the גמרא learns that meat is properly eaten at night, as long as there is good light. Several pairs of פסוקים are reconciled: בינונים died at once from the quail while רשעים suffered for a month; the מן tasted like bread, oil or honey depending on the eater's age; and there was dew both under and over the מן, like a box. רבי יהושע בן קרחה reads שטוח as שחוט, but רבי says birds and שחיטה are known from other פסוקים, so for him שטוח means the מן fell in layers. The גמרא then tells of the four kinds of quail and of later חכמים who received quail, including רבא, who realized his quail had come in רב חסדא's merit. Finally, the תנאים discuss whether the מן was absorbed into all 248 limbs, and they disagree about why the תורה commands a peg for relieving oneself: either the waste came from outside food, or it was needed only after the sin. The amud ends by opening another explanation of 'לחם אבירים אכל איש', which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Bread was requested properly, so it came properly
steps.stepSummary: Unlike the meat, the bread (מן) was a proper request, so it was given in a proper way, in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bread, which they asked for properly, was given to them properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a contrast from the previous lines. The meat request was improper, but the bread request was proper, so the bread came at a proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread is a basic need, so asking for it was reasonable. Because of that, the מן came in the morning, when there was a full day to prepare and eat it. This sets up the next line, which learns a lesson from the meat coming at night instead.

phrases.english: Bread, which they asked for properly —
phrases.notes: Bread is a necessity, so the request was legitimate.

phrases.english: was given to them properly.
phrases.notes: It came in the morning, with time to prepare it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לחם ששאלו כהוגן ניתן להם כהוגן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast, begun on the previous amud, between the improper request for meat and the proper request for bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bread was a proper request and was given properly, in the morning.

steps.title: The Torah teaches eating meat at night
steps.stepSummary: Since the meat came in the evening, the תורה teaches the דרך ארץ of eating meat only at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here the תורה taught proper manners: a person should eat meat only at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא learns a lesson in manners from the פסוק that the meat came in the evening. It says that meat is properly eaten at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'בתת ה׳ לכם בערב בשר לאכול,' so the meat came in the evening. The גמרא takes this timing as a model of proper behavior. Bread is the daytime staple, and meat belongs to the evening meal.

phrases.english: From here the Torah taught proper conduct,
that a person should not eat meat
except at night.
phrases.notes: Learned from the meat coming 'בערב,' in the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical lesson from the timing contrast in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat should properly be eaten at night.

steps.title: אביי says a meal should be eaten in daytime
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the night-meat lesson using אביי's teaching that a meal should be eaten in daylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't אביי say: someone who has a meal should eat it only in the daytime!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the lesson from step 2. אביי taught that meals belong in the daytime, which seems to contradict eating meat at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reason is that a person should see what he is eating. If meals should be eaten by day, it is hard to say that meat should properly be eaten at night. The two teachings appear to clash.

phrases.english: But didn't Abaye say:
one who has a meal —
should eat it only in the daytime!
phrases.notes: So that he can see what he is eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lesson drawn in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that meat should be eaten only at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי requires meals to be eaten by day, which contradicts eating meat at night.

steps.title: Daytime means daylight-like conditions
steps.stepSummary: אביי did not mean actual daytime, only conditions like daytime, where one can see.
steps.simpleTranslation: We mean 'like daytime.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. אביי's 'daytime' really means good light, so a night meal in good light is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's concern is being able to see the food. A meal at night with enough light meets that concern. So eating meat at night, in good light, already satisfies אביי's 'ביממא', and the two teachings do not conflict.

phrases.english: We are saying: like daytime.
phrases.notes: Enough light to see what one eats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3 by reinterpreting אביי's word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי required meals in literal daytime.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי only required daylight-like conditions, meaning good light, so a night meal is acceptable.
steps.whatToRemember: Meat is properly eaten at night, and אביי's 'daytime' only means having enough light to see the food.

steps.title: משה set fixed mealtimes
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says that at first בני ישראל ate randomly, like chickens, until משה set fixed mealtimes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: At first, Israel was like chickens pecking in the garbage, until משה came and set a mealtime for them.
steps.whatsHappening: An additional teaching on the same theme: משה established set times to eat, morning and evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, people grabbed food whenever they found it, like chickens pecking at scraps. The bread in the morning and the meat in the evening created fixed, dignified mealtimes.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
At first, Israel was like chickens
that peck in the garbage,
phrases.notes: They ate whenever they found food.

phrases.english: until Moshe came
and set for them a mealtime.
phrases.notes: Morning (bread) and evening (meat).

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אחא בר יעקב בתחלה היו ישראל דומין כתרנגולים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching about the timing of meals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה established fixed mealtimes for בני ישראל.

steps.title: Two verses disagree on when they died
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק says they died with meat still between their teeth, and another speaks of a full month. How do these fit together?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The meat was still between their teeth,' and it is written 'for a month of days.' How can this be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the שליו and points out two פסוקים that seem to contradict each other about when the punishment came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: במדבר י״א:ל״ג implies immediate death, before the meat was even chewed. במדבר י״א:כ׳ says they would eat it for a month until it disgusted them. Both cannot seem to be true for the same people.

phrases.english: 'The meat was still between their teeth,'
phrases.notes: This sounds like they died right away.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'for a month of days,'
phrases.notes: This sounds like they kept eating for a whole month.

phrases.english: How can this be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the punishment of the quail-eaters.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים describing the punishment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק implies instant death, and the other implies a month-long period.

steps.title: Average people died at once, the wicked suffered a month
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים describe different groups: בינונים died immediately, and רשעים suffered for a month first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The average people died immediately. The wicked kept suffering for a month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each פסוק to a different group of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'still between their teeth' פסוק refers to the בינונים, who were spared drawn-out suffering. The 'month' פסוק refers to the רשעים, whose punishment was longer and harsher.

keyTerms.meaning: average people, neither fully righteous nor wicked

phrases.english: The average people died immediately.
The wicked kept suffering
for a month of days.
phrases.notes: And then they died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים describe the same people.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each פסוק describes a different group: בינונים died immediately, and רשעים died after a month.
steps.whatToRemember: The quail punishment differed by level: בינונים died at once, and רשעים suffered for a month.

steps.title: ריש לקיש reads וישטחו as וישחטו
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rereads 'they spread' as 'they slaughtered,' teaching that ישראל became liable to be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they spread them out' — ריש לקיש said: Don't read 'וישטחו' but 'וישחטו.' This teaches that the enemies of Israel became liable to slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש makes a דרשה by swapping letters in a word from the quail story, to hint at the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters ט and ח are swapped, turning 'spread' into 'slaughtered.' 'The enemies of Israel' is a polite way of saying ישראל themselves. Their improper demand made them deserve death.

keyTerms.meaning: do not read [it as] — a letter-change דרשה
the enemies of Israel (a euphemism for ישראל)

steps.confusionAlert: 'שונאיהן של ישראל' does not mean actual enemies. It is a euphemism that avoids saying something bad directly about ישראל.

phrases.english: 'And they spread out' — Reish Lakish said:
Do not read 'vayishtechu,'
but rather 'vayishchatu' —
phrases.notes: The letters ט and ח are switched.

phrases.english: this teaches that they became liable,
the enemies of Israel, to slaughter.
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying ישראל themselves, without saying it outright.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new דרשה on another word in the quail פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל became liable to death because of their improper demand for meat.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה reads שטוח as שחוט
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rereads 'spread out' as 'slaughtered,' teaching that food needing שחיטה fell together with the מן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Spread out' — it was taught in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: Don't read 'שטוח' but 'שחוט.' This teaches that something requiring שחיטה came down to Israel with the מן.
steps.whatsHappening: A second letter-swap דרשה on a similar word. This one teaches that birds requiring שחיטה fell together with the מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This דרשה uses the same ט/ח swap as step 8, but for a different point. Here it is not about punishment but about what came down: meat, meaning birds, that needed שחיטה. This sets up רבי's objection in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in the name of

phrases.aramaic: ״שָׁטוֹחַ״, תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קָרְחָה:
phrases.english: 'Spread out' — it was taught in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha:
Do not read 'shatoach,' but rather 'shachut,'

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁיָּרַד לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עִם הַמָּן
phrases.english: this teaches that there came down to Israel, with the manna,
something that requires slaughter.
phrases.notes: Birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel letter-swap דרשה on a similar word, with a different lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds requiring שחיטה fell together with the מן.

steps.title: רבי objects: this is already explicit
steps.stepSummary: רבי objects that there is no need to change the word, because a פסוק in תהלים already says plainly that meat and birds rained down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: Do you learn it from here? Doesn't it already say: 'He rained meat upon them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the sea'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי challenges רבי יהושע בן קרחה's דרשה. Why rework a word when another פסוק already states the point openly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'אל תקרי' דרשה is unnecessary if the idea is written explicitly elsewhere. תהלים ע״ח:כ״ז already says birds rained down. So רבי concludes that 'שטוח' must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: do you learn it from here? (it is unnecessary)

phrases.english: Rebbi said:
And do you learn it from here?
Hasn't it already been stated:
'He rained upon them meat like dust,'
'and winged birds like the sand (of the sea).'
phrases.notes: תהלים ע״ח:כ״ז.

steps.triggerLanguage: וכי מכאן אתה למד והלא כבר נאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the דרשה in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reading of שטוח as שחוט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no need to alter a word to teach what another פסוק states explicitly.

steps.title: רבי's source that משה was taught שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי learns the laws of שחיטה from 'וזבחת כאשר צויתיך,' so he does not need 'שטוח' for שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: רבי says, 'You shall slaughter as I have commanded you' teaches that משה was commanded about the esophagus and the windpipe: the majority of one in a bird, and the majority of both in an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that, for רבי, the laws of שחיטה come from a different פסוק. This supports his refusal to use 'שטוח' for שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כאשר צויתיך' refers to oral instructions given to משה. These include which pipes to cut and how much: most of one pipe for a bird, and most of both for an animal. Since שחיטה is covered here, 'שטוח' is free to teach something else.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a key source that the details of שחיטה are a commandment given to משה, including the rule of cutting most of one סימן for a bird and most of both סימנים for an animal.

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rebbi says:
'You shall slaughter as I have commanded you,'
phrases.notes: דברים י״ב:כ״א.

phrases.english: this teaches that Moshe was commanded
about the esophagus and the windpipe,
about the majority of one in a bird,
and about the majority of both in an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: ותניא רבי אומר וזבחת כאשר צויתיך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי's position from step 10 with his own source for שחיטה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's view that 'שטוח' is not needed to teach about שחיטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'וזבחת כאשר צויתיך' teaches the laws of שחיטה given to משה.

steps.title: רבי: שטוח means the מן fell in layers
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי, 'שטוח' teaches that the מן came down in spread-out layers.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what does 'שטוח' teach? It teaches that it came down for them in layers upon layers.
steps.whatsHappening: Having freed the word from teaching שחיטה, רבי gives 'שטוח' its own meaning: the food fell in neat spread-out layers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads 'שטוח' plainly as 'spread out,' with no letter change. It describes how the food fell, in flat layers, rather than hinting at שחיטה. This completes רבי's alternative to רבי יהושע בן קרחה.

keyTerms.meaning: what does the verse come to teach?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן קרחה reads שטוח as שחוט, meaning birds needing שחיטה fell with the מן. רבי rejects this, because the birds are explicit in תהלים and שחיטה comes from 'וזבחת כאשר צויתיך.' For רבי, שטוח means the food fell in layers.

phrases.english: Rather, what does the verse teach by saying 'shatoach'?
It teaches that it came down for them
in layers upon layers.
phrases.notes: Read plainly, with no letter change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי's alternative reading after showing שחיטה is learned elsewhere.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי, 'שטוח' means the food fell in layers, not that it required שחיטה.

steps.title: Three different descriptions of the manna's taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the תורה describes the מן as bread, as oil, and as honey, which seem to contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'bread,' it is written 'oil,' and it is written 'honey.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up three פסוקים that describe the מן in three different ways. This sets up the question of which description is correct, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק calls the מן 'bread,' another says it tasted like 'oil,' and a third says it tasted like 'honey.' If the מן had one fixed taste, these descriptions clash. The גמרא states the clash without a question word, but the pattern 'כתיב X וכתיב Y' is a standard way of raising a contradiction.
steps.confusionAlert: There is no explicit question here, but 'כתיב… וכתיב…' is the גמרא's classic way of saying 'these פסוקים seem to contradict each other.'

phrases.english: It is written 'bread,'
phrases.notes: שמות טז:ד – 'I will rain down bread from heaven'

phrases.english: and it is written 'oil,'
phrases.notes: במדבר יא:ח – its taste was like the taste of cake made with oil

phrases.english: and it is written 'honey.'
phrases.notes: שמות טז:לא – its taste was like a wafer made with honey

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from how the מן fell to what the מן tasted like.
steps.kashyaTarget: The descriptions of the מן's taste in the פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three פסוקים give three different tastes for one food, so they seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: Each age group tasted something different
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that the מן tasted like bread for young men, like oil for the elderly, and like honey for small children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: for young men it was bread, for old people it was oil, and for little children it was honey.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא resolves the contradiction from the last step. All three פסוקים are true, each for a different group of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מן adjusted itself to whoever ate it. Strong young people got filling bread, old people got soft, rich oil, and small children got sweet honey. So the פסוקים do not argue with each other; each one describes a different person's experience.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
For the youths — bread,
for the elderly — oil,
for the small children — honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק describes a different group of eaters
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מן had one taste, so the three descriptions conflict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מן's taste changed to suit each age group, so all three פסוקים are correct.

steps.title: Why is the word for quail written one way and read another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the word for quail is written with a ש (שליו) but read with a ס (סליו).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'שליו,' and we read it 'סליו'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the מן to the quail. It asks why the written spelling of the word differs from how it is pronounced, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the כתיב (written form) and the קרי (read form) differ, חז"ל assume each form carries its own lesson. The question is what each spelling is meant to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Quail. The written form, which hints at שַׁלְוָה (peace)
Quail as it is pronounced, which hints at thorns

phrases.english: It is written 'shlav' (with a shin),
and we read it 'slav' (with a samekh)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the מן to the second food of the מדבר, the quail.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson do the two different forms of the word teach?

steps.title: Peace for the righteous, thorns for the wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that צדיקים ate the quail in peace (שלוה), while רשעים felt it was like thorns (סילוין).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: the righteous eat it in peace and calm, and the wicked eat it and it feels to them like thorns.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question about the spelling. Each form of the word describes how a different kind of person experienced the quail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The written ש points to שלוה (calm), which is how the righteous ate. The spoken ס points to סילוין (thorns), which is what it felt like to the wicked. This connects to the פסוק in במדבר where those who craved meat were punished while it was still between their teeth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
The righteous eat it in tranquility,
phrases.notes: This comes from the word being written with a ש.

phrases.english: the wicked eat it
and it seems to them like thorns.
phrases.notes: This comes from the word being pronounced like a ס.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: צַדִּיקִים אוֹכְלִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשַׁלְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two spellings describe two experiences: calm for צדיקים and thorns for רשעים.

steps.title: Four kinds of quail, from best to worst
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא lists four kinds of quail and says שיכלי is the best and שליו is the worst.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רבא said: there are four kinds of quail: שיכלי, קיבלי, פסיוני, and שליו. The best of all is שיכלי, and the worst of all is שליו.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement gives more information about quail. It lists four types and ranks them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list sets up the next step's point. The שליו that ישראל ate in the מדבר was the lowest of the four types, yet the next step shows how amazing even that one was.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanan bar Rava said:
There are four kinds of quail,
and these are they: sikhli, and kivli,
and pasyoni, and slav.
The best of all of them: sikhli,
the worst of all of them: slav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא: אַרְבָּעָה מִינֵי סְלָיו הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further information about the quail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four kinds of quail. שיכלי is the best and שליו is the worst.

steps.title: How rich even the lowest quail was
steps.stepSummary: The quail was as small as a sparrow but swelled to fill the oven, and its fat soaked through thirteen loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was like a small bird. They would put it in the oven, and it swelled until it filled the oven. They would put it on top of thirteen loaves, and even the last loaf could only be eaten mixed with something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes how amazing the quail of the מדבר was, even though it was the 'worst' of the four kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny bird grew to fill a whole oven. Its fat dripped through thirteen stacked loaves, so even the bottom loaf was too rich to eat plain and had to be mixed with other food. The point is that even the lowest type was extraordinarily rich.

keyTerms.meaning: A small bird, like a sparrow

phrases.english: And it was like a small sparrow,
and we would place it in the oven
and it would swell and fill the oven,
and we would place it upon thirteen loaves,
and the last one could not be eaten
except through mixing with other food.
phrases.notes: It was so soaked with fat that it was too rich to eat alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how rich even the 'worst' kind of quail from step 17 was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the lowest kind of quail was extraordinarily large and rich.

steps.title: Quail found by רב יהודה and רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה found quail among his wine barrels, and רב חסדא found quail among his wood logs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה would find quail among the barrels, and רב חסדא would find quail among the logs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells stories showing that great אמוראים also received quail miraculously in their own time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quail appeared in unusual places, among wine barrels and among firewood, as a sign of these חכמים' merit. The mention of רב חסדא sets up the story about רבא that follows.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה מִשְׁתְּכַח לֵיהּ בֵּי דַנֵּי,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda would find quail among the barrels,

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא מִשְׁתְּכַח לֵיהּ בֵּי צִיבֵי.
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda would find quail among the logs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה מִשְׁתְּכַח לֵיהּ בֵּי דַנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the quail of the מדבר to quail that appeared to later חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה and רב חסדא each received quail in a miraculous way.

steps.title: The day the quail stopped coming to רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבא's sharecropper brought him a quail every day. One day he did not, so רבא went up to the roof and heard a child say a פסוק about trembling at bad news.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא's sharecropper would bring him quail every day. One day he did not bring it. רבא said: 'What is this?' He went up to the roof and heard a child saying the פסוק 'I heard, and my insides trembled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story builds suspense. The quail stops coming, and רבא looks for the reason. He hears a child's פסוק as a sign, and the next step explains what he understood from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing a child's פסוק was treated as a kind of message. The פסוק from חבקוק speaks of terrible news, which tells רבא that something bad has happened and explains the missing quail.

keyTerms.meaning: His sharecropper (a worker who farms the owner's field for a share of the crop)

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא מַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ אֲרִיסֵיהּ כׇּל יוֹמָא.
phrases.english: Rava's sharecropper would bring him quail every day.
One day he did not bring it.
He said: What is this?
He went up to the roof,
he heard a child who was saying:
'I heard, and my insides trembled.'
phrases.notes: חבקוק ג:טז – a reaction to terrible news

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא מַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ אֲרִיסֵיהּ כׇּל יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quail stories with רבא, a student of רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the quail stopped, רבא heard a פסוק about bad news.

steps.title: The student ate in his teacher's merit
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that רב חסדא has died, since he had been receiving quail only in his teacher's merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Learn from this that רב חסדא has died, and the student was eating because of the teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא puts the clues together. The missing quail and the child's פסוק mean that his teacher רב חסדא has passed away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's daily quail had not come from his own merit but from רב חסדא's. Once רב חסדא died, the quail stopped. A student benefits from his רבי's זכות.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul came to rest (he passed away)

steps.whatToRemember: The מן tasted different to each age group, and the quail was experienced differently by צדיקים and רשעים. Later חכמים also received quail, and רבא learned that he had received it only in his teacher רב חסדא's merit.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story teaches humility and the bond between a student and his רבי. Blessings a student receives can come from his teacher's זכות.

phrases.english: He said: Learn from this
that Rav Ḥisda has passed away,
and on account of the teacher the student was eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִנֵּיהּ נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the clues in step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא received quail in רב חסדא's merit, and when it stopped he knew his teacher had died.

steps.title: Two verses about the dew seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק says the dew went up off the מן, which means the dew was on top. Another says the מן fell onto the dew, which means the dew was underneath.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And the layer of dew lifted,' and it is also written: 'And when the dew fell.' Which is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out two פסוקים about the מן that seem to clash. It is setting up the next step, which will resolve them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמות, the dew 'lifted' and the מן was revealed, so the dew covered the מן from above. In במדבר, the dew fell first and then the מן landed on it, so the dew was below. Both cannot seem true at once.

keyTerms.meaning: And when the dew came down

phrases.english: It is written: 'And the layer of dew lifted,'
phrases.notes: שמות טז:יד. The dew is on top of the מן.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And when the dew fell'?
phrases.notes: במדבר יא:ט. The מן falls onto the dew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the quail back to the topic of the מן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים describing the dew and the מן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק places the dew above the מן and the other places it below.

steps.title: Dew above and dew below, like a box
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers that there was dew both above and below the מן, so it sat as if packed in a box.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא said: There was dew above and dew below, and the manna looked as if it were placed in a box.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא resolves the contradiction by saying both פסוקים are true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First a layer of dew fell, then the מן, then another layer of dew on top. The bottom layer matches 'when the dew fell,' and the top layer matches 'the dew lifted.' The מן was protected like something packed in a case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Dew above, and dew below,
and it looked like something placed in a box.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both verses describe different layers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dew had to be either only above or only below.
steps.terutzMaskana: There were two layers of dew, one under and one over the מן.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: it melted on the palm of the hand
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains the word מחוספס as 'something that dissolves on the palm of the hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Fine and flaky (מחוספס)': ריש לקיש said: A substance that melted on the palm of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a strange word used to describe the מן, and ריש לקיש explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש splits the word into parts: מח (melt) and פס (palm). The מן was so delicate that it dissolved when it touched the hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Flaky or fine (the word being explained)

phrases.english: 'Fine and flaky,'
phrases.notes: שמות טז:יד

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A thing that dissolves on the palm of the hand.
phrases.notes: מח = melts, פס = palm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New discussion of another word in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחוספס means the מן dissolved on the palm.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: absorbed into all 248 limbs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says מחוספס hints that the מן was absorbed into all 248 limbs of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A substance that was absorbed into the 248 limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second explanation of מחוספס, based on the number value of its letters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the word through גימטריא and says it equals 248, the number of limbs in a person. His point is that the מן was fully absorbed into the body, so there was no waste.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁנִּבְלָע בְּמָאתַיִם וְאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה אֵבָרִים.
phrases.english: A thing that is absorbed into the 248 limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same word than ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחוספס, read as a number, hints that the מן was absorbed into all 248 limbs.

steps.title: But the number is too big
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the letters of מחוספס add up to more than 248.
steps.simpleTranslation: מחוספס is much more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's math.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spelled with a ו, the word is מ(40) ח(8) ו(6) ס(60) פ(80) ס(60), which equals 254, not 248. So the hint seems not to work.

phrases.english: 'Mechuspas' comes to much more!
phrases.notes: Spelled with a ו, the letters add up to 254.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's number reading.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The letters add up to 254, not 248.

steps.title: It is written without a ו
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that in the תורה the word is spelled without a ו, so it equals exactly 248.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: 'מחספס' is written (without a vav).
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends רבי יוחנן by pointing to the exact spelling in the ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the ו, the letters are 40+8+60+80+60 = 248. The objection only worked because it used the full spelling, while the תורה uses the short one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written מחספס (short spelling, no ו)
A word spelled without an optional letter

steps.whatToRemember: The מן was so pure that it was fully absorbed into the body. The spelling מחספס = 248 hints at this.
steps.confusionAlert: The two spellings differ by one letter, the ו: מְחוּסְפָּס (with ו, 254) versus מְחֻסְפָּס (without ו, 248). The objection in step 26 counted the full spelling. רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that the תורה spells it without the ו.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
'Mechuspas' is written (without a vav).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מְחֻסְפָּס כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the math objection in step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word is spelled with a ו and equals 254.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah spells it without a ו, so it equals 248.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the bread the angels eat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבי עקיבא explains 'לחם אבירים' as bread eaten by the angels.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Man ate the bread of the mighty (אבירים)': bread that the ministering angels eat. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with רבי עקיבא's explanation of a פסוק in תהלים about the מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads אבירים ('mighty ones') as referring to the angels. In his view, the מן was the same food the angels eat in heaven.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Man ate the bread of the mighty,'
phrases.notes: תהלים עח:כה

phrases.english: bread that the ministering angels eat,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן לֶחֶם אַבִּירִים אָכַל אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new source about the nature of the מן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבירים refers to angels, so the מן was angels' food.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: angels do not eat bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says רבי עקיבא erred, because משה said that in heaven he did not eat bread, which shows that heavenly beings do not eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: When these words were said before רבי ישמעאל, he said to them: Go and tell עקיבא: עקיבא, you erred! Do the ministering angels eat bread? Has it not already been said: 'Bread I did not eat and water I did not drink'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל strongly challenges רבי עקיבא's explanation, using a פסוק about משה רבינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When משה was in heaven for forty days, he did not eat or drink. If a person in heaven does not need food, then the angels themselves certainly do not eat bread. So 'angels' bread' cannot be the meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so? (a challenging question)
But has it not already been said

phrases.english: And when these words were said before Rabbi Yishmael,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: צְאוּ וְאִמְרוּ לוֹ לַעֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: he said to them: Go out and say to Akiva:
Akiva, you have erred!
Do the ministering angels eat bread?
But has it not already been said:
'Bread I did not eat and water I did not drink'!
phrases.notes: דברים ט:ט, said by משה on the mountain.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲקִיבָא טָעִיתָ וְכִי מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹכְלִין לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי עקיבא's reading from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's claim that angels eat bread.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even משה did not eat in heaven, so angels surely do not eat.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: bread absorbed into the limbs
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל reads אבירים as אברים (limbs): bread that was absorbed into all 248 limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how do I explain 'אבירים'? Bread that was absorbed into the 248 limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבי עקיבא's reading, רבי ישמעאל offers his own explanation of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links אבירים to the similar-sounding אברים (limbs). This matches רבי יוחנן's idea in step 25 that the מן was fully absorbed and left no waste.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain (this word or verse)?

phrases.english: Rather, how do I explain 'abirim'?

phrases.aramaic: לֶחֶם שֶׁנִּבְלַע בְּמָאתַיִם וְאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה אֵבָרִים.
phrases.english: Bread that was absorbed into the 248 limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי עקיבא's reading with a new one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבירים = אברים: the מן was absorbed into all the limbs.

steps.title: Then why did they need to go outside to relieve themselves?
steps.stepSummary: If the מן left no waste, why does the תורה command carrying a peg and going outside the camp to relieve oneself?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain: 'And you shall have a peg among your weapons (and you shall go out there, outside)'?
steps.whatsHappening: A difficulty is raised against the 'no waste' reading. The first-person 'מה אני מקיים' may mean רבי ישמעאל is still speaking inside the ברייתא, or it may be the גמרא asking. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives rules for the camp in the desert about digging and covering waste outside the camp. If the מן was fully absorbed, these rules would seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall go out there, outside (to relieve yourself)

phrases.english: But then how do I explain:
'And you shall have a peg among your weapons,'
phrases.notes: דברים כג:יד

phrases.english: '(and you shall go out there, outside)',
phrases.notes: דברים כג:יג

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים וְיָתֵד תִּהְיֶה לְךָ עַל אֲזֵנֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'no waste' idea from step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the מן was fully absorbed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה assumes there was waste in the desert camp.

steps.title: The waste came from food bought from gentile merchants
steps.stepSummary: The waste came from other foods that gentile merchants sold to בני ישראל, not from the מן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Things that the merchants of the nations of the world sold to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The difficulty is answered: the rules about waste refer to other food, not to the מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בני ישראל sometimes bought regular food from passing gentile traders. That food produced waste. The מן itself still left none, so the explanation that the מן was fully absorbed stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The מן was a perfect food, absorbed into all 248 limbs. Any waste in the desert came from regular food bought from gentile traders.

phrases.english: Things that the merchants of the nations of the world
would sell to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבָרִים שֶׁתַּגָּרֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מוֹכְרִין אוֹתָן לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the verse to a different case (other food).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The waste rules show that the מן produced waste.
steps.terutzMaskana: The waste came from bought food. The מן left none.

steps.title: The manna dissolved even the merchants' food
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא says the מן made even food bought from gentile merchants leave no waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא says: Even food that gentile merchants sold to them, the מן dissolved it completely.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion disagrees with the answer we just heard. רבי אלעזר בן פרטא says the outside food did not produce waste either, because the מן dissolved it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 said the waste came from the merchants' food, not from the מן. רבי אלעזר בן פרטא rejects that: the מן was so powerful that it absorbed the other food too. That means the merchants cannot explain the peg-verse, so he will need a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: dissolves them / makes them fully digested
merchants of the nations of the world (gentile traders)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Perata says:
even items that the merchants of the nations of the world
would sell to them —
the manna dissolved them.
phrases.notes: The מן caused even other food to be absorbed with no waste.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פַּרְטָא אוֹמֵר: אַף דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the answer in step 32 that the merchants' food caused the waste.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מן dissolved even the outside food, so nothing produced waste.

steps.title: Then what is the peg verse for?
steps.stepSummary: If nothing produced waste, why does the תורה command carrying a peg to relieve oneself?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק: 'And you shall have a peg among your weapons'?
steps.whatsHappening: The question from step 31 comes back, now aimed at רבי אלעזר בן פרטא. This line sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אלעזר בן פרטא said even the merchants' food left no waste, the old answer no longer works. So the פסוק about the peg seems pointless according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: how do I fulfill / explain (a verse)?
a peg / small spade for digging

phrases.english: But how do I explain
'And you shall have a peg among your weapons' —
phrases.notes: דברים כג:יד, the command to dig and cover waste outside the camp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new view of step 33 using the peg-verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא's claim that nothing produced waste.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there was no waste at all, the תורה's command to carry a peg for relieving oneself would have no purpose.

steps.title: After they sinned, they had to walk three parasangs
steps.stepSummary: After בני ישראל sinned, the מן lost this power, and הקב"ה made them walk up to three פרסאות to relieve themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they sinned, הקב"ה said: I had said they would be like the ministering angels; now I will make them trouble themselves to walk three פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא answers: the peg-verse applies to the time after the sin. Then they did produce waste, and had to walk far out of the camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original plan was that בני ישראל would be like angels, with no waste. After they sinned, this blessing was taken away, and the command of the peg became necessary. The walk of three פרסאות was itself a kind of punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: parasangs (a unit of distance, about 4 מיל)

phrases.english: After they sinned
the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I said they would be like the ministering angels,
now I will trouble them
to walk three parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַחַר שֶׁסָּרְחוּ אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Time-based split: the verse refers to the period after the sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The peg-verse shows there was always waste.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before the sin there was no waste; after the sin there was, and they had to walk out of the camp.

steps.title: Proof that the camp was three parasangs long
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק plus רבה בר בר חנה's eyewitness report show the camp stretched three פרסאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'They camped by the Jordan, from בית הישימות to אבל השטים.' And רבה בר בר חנה said: I myself saw that place, and it was three פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves where the number 'three פרסאות' comes from. It shows the camp was that long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives the two ends of the camp. רבה בר בר חנה saw the area and measured it as three פרסאות. This supports the claim that some people had to walk that far.

phrases.english: As it is written:
'And they camped by the Jordan
from Beth-Jeshimoth to Abel-shittim',
phrases.notes: במדבר לג:מט.

phrases.english: and Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
I myself saw that place
and it was three parasangs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the 'three פרסאות' in step 35.
steps.raayaObject: The camp was three פרסאות long.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר לג:מט plus רבה בר בר חנה's eyewitness report.

steps.title: They relieved themselves only behind the camp
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches they went only behind the camp, so people at the front had to walk the full length.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא taught: When they relieved themselves, they did not go in front of the camp or to its sides, only behind it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second piece to the proof. Since they always went behind the camp, people at the front had to cross the whole camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A long camp alone does not prove that anyone walked three פרסאות. This ברייתא completes the picture: everyone had to go to the back, so those at the front walked the full three פרסאות.

phrases.english: And it was taught: When they relieved themselves,
they would not relieve themselves in front of them,
nor to their sides,
but only behind them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 36.
steps.raayaObject: Some people had to walk the full three פרסאות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that they relieved themselves only behind the camp.

steps.title: The people's complaint shows the manna left no waste
steps.stepSummary: בני ישראל feared the מן would swell inside them because it produced no waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But now our soul is dry, there is nothing at all.' They said: This מן will eventually swell in our stomachs. Is there anyone born of a woman who takes food in and does not let it out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show that the מן really produced no waste. The people's complaint only makes sense if nothing came out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people worried that food going in without coming out would make their stomachs swell and hurt them. That fear proves they saw that the מן left no waste. This supports the whole idea that the מן was fully absorbed.

keyTerms.meaning: one born of a woman (a human being)
takes in but does not let out

phrases.english: 'But now our soul is dry, there is nothing at all.'
phrases.notes: במדבר יא:ו.

phrases.english: They said: This manna will eventually
swell in their stomachs,
is there anyone born of a woman
who takes in but does not expel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds proof from a different פסוק to the basic idea that the מן left no waste.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר יא:ו and the people's complaint about it.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: absorbed into 248 limbs
steps.stepSummary: In a parallel version, רבי ישמעאל reads אבירים as איברים: the מן was absorbed into all 248 limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: When these words were said before רבי ישמעאל, he said to them: Do not read 'אבירים', but 'איברים': something absorbed into 248 limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי ישמעאל's response to these teachings. He agrees the מן was fully absorbed, reading the word as 'limbs.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats רבי ישמעאל's reading from step 30, but now as a response to this discussion. It sets up his own explanation of the peg-verse, which differs from רבי אלעזר בן פרטא's.

keyTerms.meaning: do not read (it as), a re-reading of a word

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a copying mistake. The גמרא is bringing a parallel version where רבי ישמעאל responds to these teachings, so his reading appears again for a new purpose.

phrases.english: And when these words were said before Rabbi Yishmael,
he said to them: Do not read 'abirim',
but rather 'eivarim' (limbs) —
something that was absorbed
in two hundred and forty-eight limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings רבי ישמעאל's view in response to the discussion, returning to his reading from step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מן was fully absorbed into all 248 limbs.

steps.title: The peg verse, asked of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: If the מן was fully absorbed, what is the peg-verse for, according to רבי ישמעאל?
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do I explain 'And you shall have a peg among your weapons'?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question about the peg-verse is now asked according to רבי ישמעאל. This line sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מן left no waste, the command to carry a peg seems unneeded. רבי ישמעאל must explain where waste came from.

phrases.english: But how do I explain
'And you shall have a peg among your weapons' —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ישמעאל's view from step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's claim that the מן was fully absorbed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A total lack of waste makes the peg-verse seem pointless.

steps.title: The waste came from food brought from overseas
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says the peg-verse refers to waste from food brought from overseas, not from the מן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to the food that came to them from overseas lands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers that the outside food did produce waste. That is why the peg was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the answer of step 32 and disagrees with רבי אלעזר בן פרטא. For רבי ישמעאל, the מן only dissolved itself, not other food. So the outside food explains the peg-verse even before any sin.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees the מן itself left no waste. They argue about the peg-verse: רבי ישמעאל says waste came from outside food; רבי אלעזר בן פרטא says the מן dissolved even that, and the peg was needed only after the sin.

phrases.english: With the items that came to them
from overseas lands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-of-waste split: waste came from outside food, not the מן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The peg-verse means the מן produced waste.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the imported food produced waste; the מן was fully absorbed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ישמעאל and רבי אלעזר בן פרטא disagree on whether the מן also dissolved outside food.

steps.title: Opening a new reading of the verse about the bread of the mighty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a דבר אחר, a new way to read "לחם אבירים אכל איש" (תהלים עח:כה), setting up the next explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: "Man (איש) did eat the bread of the mighty."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes the same verse again and signals that a new interpretation is coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the focus was on the word אבירים: angels, or limbs (איברים). The phrase דבר אחר tells us we are not continuing the earlier argument. A separate reading of this verse is about to begin, and the explanation itself comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation; introduces a different interpretation of the same verse
Bread of the mighty; the verse's description of the מן
A man; the word in the verse that may be read in a new way

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not contain the new explanation yet. It only re-quotes the verse. Do not think the גמרא is repeating the earlier אבירים discussion; the new idea comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
phrases.notes: Here comes a whole new way to read the same verse.

phrases.english: "Man did eat the bread of the mighty"
phrases.notes: תהלים עח:כה. The verse is quoted again to give it a new reading.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: לֶחֶם אַבִּירִים אָכַל אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי ישמעאל discussion about absorption and waste. Returns to the same verse to open a separate interpretation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This is only a setup statement. It re-quotes the verse to introduce an alternative interpretation, which comes in the next line.
